surface_mechanism_description: Ligand exchange between TMA and surface hydroxyl groups followed by water pulse to regenerate OH sites. At higher temperatures, HF can fluorinate the underlying Al2O3 substrate to form an AlF3 layer. TMA can accept fluorine from the AlF3 layer in a ligand-exchange reaction to form volatile AlF(CH3)2 species that desorb from the surface, leading to AlF3 etching.
evidence: The text describes the reaction equations and surface mechanisms in detail. It mentions the formation of AlF(CH3)2* and AlF2(CH3)* species during the ligand-exchange process, as well as the presence of AlCH3* and HF* surface species.
